findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables and committed to source control. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or read access to the repo can retrieve them and impersonate the associated IAM identity.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so Lambda environment variables (which here hold secrets) are encrypted only with the AWS-managed default key rather than a customer-managed CMK, providing no separate key-policy access boundary or auditability over the secret material.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the execution environment exposed to unpatched vulnerabilities.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network boundary controls, easing data exfiltration if the function or its embedded credentials are abused.
